notes: Twenty unique foundational price-observation and indicator mathematics topics with discrete hypothetical cases. These are candidate explanations, not individually signed-off editorials, approved assessments, or new chart algorithms.

guides.title: Candlestick body size relative to the complete range
guides.concept: A real body spans a completed candle's open and close; body-to-range expresses its magnitude relative to the high-low span, not a probability of continuation.
guides.procedure: Validate low ≤ open and close ≤ high. Compute |close−open|/(high−low)×100 only for a nonzero completed range.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Open $20.00, close $20.30, high $20.50 and low $19.50 give $0.30 body/$1.00 range = 30%, despite a bullish close.
guides.limit: A zero-range candle leaves the ratio undefined. OHLC cannot identify the order in which intrabar highs and lows occurred.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. A zero-range candle leaves the ratio undefined. OHLC cannot identify the order in which intrabar highs and lows occurred.
guides.commonError: Calling a 70% body a 70% chance of a profitable next candle.

guides.title: Upper and lower wicks do not prove execution rejection
guides.concept: A completed candle's upper wick is high−max(open,close), and lower wick is min(open,close)−low. The sizes describe the observed price envelope.
guides.procedure: State all four OHLC inputs, calculate both nonnegative wick sizes, and compare with the source interval's volume and nearby levels.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Open $10, close $10.20, high $10.70 and low $9.90 produce upper wick $0.50 and lower wick $0.10; no trader identity is established.
guides.limit: The same candle can arise through differing trade paths; wicks do not independently establish a support order or reversal.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. guides.procedure: Declare a percentage body threshold, the completed OHLC bar and minimum price increment before labeling the real body as small.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Open $10.00, close $10.01, high $10.30, low $9.70 imply body/range ≈1.67%. Whether it qualifies depends on the declared threshold.
guides.limit: A small body does not establish indecision by named traders or guarantee a next-bar reversal; prices on a wide spread can be misleading.

guides.concept: A completed session gap reflects a difference between a previous observed close and a later opening reference; it does not contain a law that price must revisit the earlier level.
guides.procedure: Mark prior session close, next-session opening bar, adjusted-data convention and extended-hours inclusion explicitly.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Previous regular-session close $10, next regular-session open $10.60: gap +$0.60, +6% against the close, before any subsequent trading.
guides.limit: Split adjustments, earnings and premarket trading can alter visual gaps; a future gap fill is unknown.

guides.title: Inside bar recognition requires two completed candle ranges
guides.concept: An inside bar's high is no higher than the previous completed high, and its low is no lower than the previous completed low under an inclusive convention.
guides.procedure: Compare current completed high and low against the immediately preceding completed high/low; state whether equality is allowed.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Prior high $10.80 and low $9.80; next high $10.60 and low $10.00 form an inclusive inside bar.
guides.limit: An unfinished bar can stop being inside, and an inside pattern does not ensure breakout direction.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. An unfinished bar can stop being inside, and an inside pattern does not ensure breakout direction.

guides.title: Swing high confirmation requires bars to its right
guides.concept: A confirmed local swing with radius r must compare a candidate high to completed neighboring bars on both sides; at the candidate timestamp those later bars were unknown.
guides.procedure: Select radius r, candidate index, strict tie policy and the full set of 2r+1 completed bars; record confirmation at index+r.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A five-bar pivot with radius two has its highest high in the middle, but that pivot cannot be confirmed until two subsequent bars close.
guides.limit: Plotting a historically confirmed pivot on its earlier candle does not imply it could have been traded with that knowledge at the earlier time.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. Plotting a historically confirmed pivot on its earlier candle does not imply it could have been traded with that knowledge at the earlier time.
guides.commonError: Using the apparent turning point before its right-side confirmation candles were completed.

guides.title: Higher-high and higher-low labels depend on confirmed pivots
guides.concept: A higher high compares two confirmed swing highs; a higher low compares two confirmed swing lows, with declared pivot rules.
guides.procedure: Record each confirmed pivot price and its later confirmation timestamp; separately calculate high-to-high and low-to-low differences.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Confirmed highs $10.20 then $10.60 are HH; confirmed lows $9.40 then $9.55 are HL, subject to identical pivot radius.
guides.limit: Pivot detection lags; right-hand confirmation bars must not be shown to a historical replay learner before their time.

guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A prior resistance boundary is $10.50. A completed close at $10.62 meets a declared close-above rule; a later close at $10.30 can show failure only when that later bar exists.
guides.limit: A single breakout can reverse; no hindsight series establishes that the first breakout observation was impossible or profitable.

guides.concept: A conventional RSI14 calculation seeds average gain and loss from fourteen completed close-to-close differences, which requires fifteen completed closes.
guides.procedure: Identify fifteen valid closes and 14 completed changes; compute mean positive/negative changes, then Wilder smooth each subsequent change.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Fourteen nonzero positive hypothetical $0.10 changes and zero losses produce RSI 100 at the seed point; the series is unavailable with only fourteen closes.
guides.limit: An RSI value cannot establish future direction; zero gain and loss needs a documented flat-series convention.

guides.title: ATR 14 first seed and Wilder recursive updates
guides.concept: Average True Range smooths true range (including gap effects) rather than high-low alone; Wilder updating gives the prior ATR thirteen-fourteenths weight.
guides.procedure: Compute true range from completed bars and prior close, seed a fourteen-bar average, then update ATR=(13×previous ATR+new TR)/14.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A seeded ATR14 of $0.40 followed by completed true range $0.68 produces (13×$0.40+$0.68)/14=$0.42.
guides.limit: ATR is measured in price units, not a directional or probability signal; vendor seed conventions and session treatment differ.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A 26-close history can first produce the slow EMA and MACD line; a 9-period SMA-seeded signal first becomes available at the 34th completed close.
guides.limit: A vendor can choose other EMA seeds or sparse-window policies; a histogram cannot be reliable before both line and signal exist.

guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A prior OBV of 1,000 shares with next close unchanged and volume 500 shares remains 1,000; a later higher close and volume 200 makes it 1,200.

guides.title: Chaikin Money Flow and zero-range candle handling
guides.concept: CMF aggregates a close-location multiplier times reported volume over a declared lookback, normalized by volume over the same window.
guides.procedure: For each completed bar with nonzero range compute ((close−low)−(high−close))/(high−low), multiply by volume, and divide window sums.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Completed high $10.50, low $9.50, close $10.25 gives close-location multiplier +0.50; with 1,000 shares its money-flow volume contribution is +500.
guides.limit: A zero high-low range requires an explicit convention; CMF is not actual order-book buy-minus-sell delta or identification of large traders.
guides.invalidation: If the input source, date/session, completed-bar status, declared window, measurement unit, formula variant or other verification requirement is missing, label the proposed interpretation unverified. A zero high-low range requires an explicit convention; CMF is not actual order-book buy-minus-sell delta or identification of large traders.
guides.commonError: Labeling CMF as exact institution-side executed volume or silently dividing by zero.

guides.concept: A fast stochastic %K measures where the latest completed close lies within a declared highest-high to lowest-low price window.
guides.procedure: Compute %K=100×(close−lowestLow)/(highestHigh−lowestLow), only with valid completed OHLC bars and positive range.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Over an illustrative complete window, highest high $11, lowest low $9 and completed close $10.50 give %K=75.
guides.limit: If highest high equals lowest low, the fraction is undefined until a documented flat-range convention; high values do not guarantee overbought reversal.

guides.procedure: Compare sum(typical bar price × bar volume)/sum(bar volume) with sum(actual print price × print shares)/sum(print shares), declaring session and inclusion rules.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: One bar with high $11, low $9, close $10 and 100 shares yields HLC3 proxy $10.00, even if the actual qualified prints were 50 shares at $9 and 50 at $11 (also $10) by coincidence.
guides.limit: Different within-bar trade distributions can give materially different exact VWAP values at identical OHLCV; the proxy does not reveal tape chronology.
